newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GTS BEGINS HUNGARY NATIONAL MICROWAVE DATA NETWORK.
newsitem.headline: GTS BEGINS HUNGARY NATIONAL MICROWAVE DATA NETWORK.

text.p: Global TeleSystems Group International (GTS) of Washington DC, unveiled plans on Monday for Central Europe's first nationwide microwave-based data transmission network.

Development of the network in conjunction with the Hungary's National Water Management Authority (OVF) will begin early in 1997. It will serve 22 Hungarian towns by the end of the next year and cover the whole of Hungary within four to five years, company officials said.

"This is the first network of its kind in Central Europe," Lou Toth, GTS's senior vice-president for Central Europe, told Reuters. "As the data transmission market opens up GTS wants to be in a position to take full advantage."
Toth said the project would represent an investment of $60 million dollars with an initial $500,000 going into a new company, Hydrotel Kft, to be set up with OVF to begin implementation.
"We expect to see an investment of around $30 million in the first two years," he said, adding that the company will use a combination of equity raises and loans to finance work.
He said GTS would take a 94 percent stake in the new company while OVF had 6 percent, but added that new investors would be welcome.
"GTS does not insist on having a full 94 percent shareholding," he said.
Toth said OVF's interest in the operation stemmed from a need to upgrade its emergency amd flood control communication system while having a decisive say in what form that upgrade takes.
He added that once OVB's needs are met there would be more than enough capacity to offer to the market.
GTS's Hungarian subsidiary, GTS Hungary, is Europe's sixth largest and central Europe's largest distributor of VSAT services (Very Small Aperture Terminal).

The company also provides rented satellite phone lines and X25 services, as well as access to Internet and Inmarsat. Its Hungarian clients are primarily banks, insurance companies, government offices and multinational companies.
